identity.name: TD POWER SYSTEMS LTD.
identity.industry: Rotating Electrical Machines — Generators for Gas/Steam/Hydro Prime Movers (power-gen capital equipment)

summary.oneLiner: TD Power Systems is an Indian manufacturer of AC generators and motors, serving global OEMs and utilities across conventional and renewable power generation, with a strong export-oriented positioning.
summary.business: TD Power Systems Limited designs and manufactures AC generators for steam, gas, hydro, and diesel power plants, alongside synchronous, induction, and traction motors for industrial and mobility applications. The company supplies to leading global OEMs, utilities, and EPC contractors, with products installed in over 113 countries. It operates manufacturing facilities in Bengaluru, India, and an international presence in Turkey.

currentContext.strengths: Established global brand with products supplied to 113 countries, indicating strong export acceptance and OEM relationships.|Diverse product portfolio spanning multiple generator and motor technologies, reducing dependence on any single power generation source.|Long-standing relationships with major global OEMs, evidenced by significant volume orders and breakthrough prototype orders in gas turbine/gas engine segments.|Engineering and manufacturing expertise enabling delivery of products meeting stringent international testing standards.
currentContext.strategies: Advance development of larger generators (40 MW to 200 MW) through UK R&D centre to expand addressable market in data centres, industrial power, and grid stability.|Implement structured Business Excellence programme (Total Quality Management, Kaizen, Quality Circles, 5S) to strengthen process discipline, productivity, and scalability.|Separate manufacturing lines for motors and generators to improve operational focus and execution efficiency.|Expand presence in hydro refurbishment and modernisation segment as an important vertical.|Sharpen manufacturing focus to support next phase of growth in motors business.|The Company declares and pays dividends in Indian rupees, subject to shareholder approval. The Board reviews capital expenditure proposals against the annual business plan, with quarterly reporting on sanctioned amounts and actuals, including variance explanations. No explicit dividend payout ratio, buyback, or debt reduction policy is stated.|Enhance energy efficiency through process optimisation and technology adoption to reduce operating costs.|Initiate utilisation of renewable energy sources and increase installation capacity as per requirement and feasibility to reduce reliance on conventional grid power during peak demand.|Account for GHG emissions across operations and value chain; actively track emissions intensity and establish company-wide reduction targets to drive continuous environmental performance improvement.
currentContext.expansion: The annual report does not detail specific new capacity expansion projects, plant additions, or commissioning timelines for TD Power Systems. The narrative focuses on industry growth outlooks for generator, steam turbine, gas turbine, and hydro generator markets, but does not outline a concrete internal capex plan for the company itself. The only investment-related note is a provision for diminution in the value of investment in its subsidiary D F Power Systems Private Limited.
currentContext.mdna: Demand for gas turbine and gas engine generators driven by AI/data centre applications in the US, distributed power, and industrial applications.|Steam turbine demand supported by captive power, biomass, waste heat recovery, and industrial applications, with increasing opportunities from the steel industry in India.|Hydro business expected to achieve one of its highest revenue contributions in the coming year, supported by a healthy pipeline of opportunities.|Motors business supported by a strong order pipeline and ongoing customer qualifications in the US and Europe.|Railway business making steady progress through ongoing supplies and qualification programmes.|Export and deemed export orders continue to dominate the order mix, accounting for a significant share of total order inflow.|Structural trends in energy infrastructure, industrial expansion, transportation modernisation, and electrification support long-term demand for generators and electric motors.|Order book of ₹1,973 Crore at year-end providing strong visibility for future growth.|Record order inflows of ₹2,238 Crore, up 51% over the previous year.|Nearly 80% of annual order inflows came from export and deemed export markets.

risks.note: Demand for generators and motors is linked to economic cycles; dependence on select markets may impact order inflow.
Revenue concentration in select segments, particularly steam turbine generators, increases exposure to demand cycles and substitution risks.
Evolving efficiency standards and rapid technological changes may affect competitiveness.
Presence of global OEMs with advanced capabilities leads to pricing and margin pressures.

one-line thesis: A pure-play generator-maker plugged deep into the global gas-turbine/engine OEM supply chain (INNIO, Baker Hughes, SpaceX projects), riding a multi-year AI-data-center + power-gen capex super-cycle with 76-79% export mix, now committing to a large-generator (up to 200MW) capacity build that opens a much bigger TAM from FY29.
financial scorecard (fy26, inr):
| Metric | FY26 | FY25 | YoY |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total income (standalone) | 17.37 bn | 12.88 bn | +35% |
| EBITDA margin (standalone, incl. other income, excl. exceptional/treasury) | 18.14% | 17.46% | +68 bps |
| PAT incl. comprehensive income (standalone) | 2.18 bn | 1.53 bn | +42% |
| Total income (consol) | 18.78 bn | 13.02 bn | +44% |
| PAT incl. comprehensive income (consol) | 2.36 bn | 1.73 bn | +36% |
| Manufacturing order book | 19.73 bn | — | — |
| FY26 order inflow | 22.38 bn | 14.78 bn | +51% |
| Q4 order inflow | 6.66 bn | — | +61% QoQ-vs-PY |
| Cash position | 1.99 bn | — | — |
| Q4 revenue | ~5.90 bn (INR590 cr) | — | — |

**One-offs:** (a) Provided INR30 mn for residual DFPS subsidiary investment → now 100% written down. (b) Turkey contract took a heavy LD (liquidated-damages) penalty due to a 1.5-month shipping delay of a component lot India→Turkey; "customer was exceptionally brutal." This cut consol gross contribution margin ~3% below the historical 33-34% average for the quarter. Mgmt calls it non-recurring (shipping no longer in their scope).
guidance:
- **FY27 revenue:** revised up to INR2,400 cr+ (24 bn+), with "extremely high probability" of a further upward revision to match Q4 inflow run-rate.
- **FY28:** capacity to address INR32 bn; mgmt expects ~INR32-33 bn on a conservative basis ("retained earnings all going into working capital").
- **Order book growth:** no formal FY28 inflow guidance, but conservatively +20-25% next year over this year.
- **Margins FY27:** in line with FY26, slightly better excluding the Turkey one-off; gross contribution to revert to ~34% historical average.
- **Q1 FY27:** progress so far suggests it will beat Q4 of last FY.
order book & pipeline:
- Mfg order book INR19.73 bn: Generators 16.77 bn · Railway 2.47 bn · Spares/aftermarket 0.2 bn · Turkey 0.29 bn.
- Export + deemed-export share of book ~76% (ex-railway).
- Q4 export inflow 80% of total (INR5.28 bn). FY26 export+deemed inflow 17.33 bn (+76% YoY); 79% of full-year inflow is exports, 21% domestic.
- Pending generator+motor order grew 66% FY26 vs FY25.
- ~INR2,000 cr of pending order to be executed this year (FY27).
segment / subsidiary:
- **Steam turbine generators:** ~25% of TDPS revenue; market growing 10-12% (captive power, biomass, waste-heat); machine sizes shifting from 30MW to 60MW range.
- **Gas turbine & gas engine generators:** "massive growth continues without pause"; large-volume orders; notable delivery into SpaceX projects; current volume orders are sub-50MW. Strong forecast through FY28.
- **Hydro:** one of TDPS's highest hydro years ahead; active in refurbishment in India and abroad; high-value wins expected this/next quarter.
- **Motors:** deprioritized in FY26 in favour of high-volume export generators; separating manufacturing lines for focus; expects stabilization and improving traction. Includes NPCIL induction-motor order (nuclear, slow/choppy ordering).
- **Railway:** orders across US, Europe, Russia + India (4 markets next year); "nothing new to report."
- **Subsidiaries:** DFPS fully written down; UK R&D sub (100%) drives large-generator technology (no royalty, captive); Turkey plant for small Turkish-market machines + EU service backup.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Large generators (up to 200MW):** the headline optionality. Existing stator line was built in 2012-13; rotor side under-invested 15 yrs ago — now investing heavily in rotor manufacturing + large machining centers. Targets export (power gen, large AI data centers, combined-cycle, potentially SMR/nuclear in ~200MW range). Detailed business plan/numbers in ~2-3 months.
- **AI data center power:** US alone ~100 GW over 5-7 yrs; could ~double globally — long cycle.
- **SMR / nuclear:** TDPS caps at ~200MW; if SMRs land in that range, addressable.
- **Aeroderivative engine generator prototype:** in progress with a customer (no specifics disclosed).
margins & cost dynamics:
- Gross contribution historically 33-34%; Q4 ~3% below due to Turkey LD; reverting to ~34%.
- RM basket: copper, forgings, electrical steel, mild steel, insulating materials (copper share not disclosed).
- Copper "drastic" (~$14,000); hedges running out → new customer prices kicking in unevenly. Protected via RM hedges + price-variation clauses.
- FX: high export exposure gives rupee-devaluation tailwind that offsets dollar/euro RM imports → broadly currency-neutral / margin-neutral.
- Sudden 10-15% commodity spikes can't be fully passed through immediately (customers won't reprice in a week); manageable for next 2-3 quarters; risk if commodities jump another 20-30%.
- Employee costs largely stable QoQ; "largely employed everyone we want" — no major additions ahead.
capex / expansion:
- ~INR50 cr capex this year + ~INR50 cr next year for debottlenecking/automation/incremental capacity (gets current facilities to ~INR30-32 bn revenue capacity, covering through FY28).
- Large-generator capex: separate, much larger, to be detailed in 2-3 months. Large machining centers have 15-16 month lead times (global machine-tool makers full) — TDPS is "a bit late." Full large-gen capacity earliest calendar '27; big ramp only calendar '28 (≈ FY29).
capital allocation:
- Strong cash INR1.99 bn maintained.
- DFPS subsidiary investment fully provided/written down (clean-up).
- Retained earnings being consumed by working capital to fund growth (inventory build for short-cycle orders → converts to cash next quarter); EBITDA→CFO conversion ~21%, expected to improve.
- Trade receivables outpaced sales growth; CFO stated the ~INR700 cr outstanding has since been fully collected.
risks & watch-items:
- Very high factory utilization → equipment-breakdown risk could cause delivery delays (the "new normal" pressure point).
- Customer concentration on a handful of prime-mover OEMs (INNIO, Baker Hughes/Brush, etc.); demand entirely derivative of OEM capacity adds (1 turbine = 1 generator).
- Commodity (copper) spikes outrunning hedges/PVC clauses.
- Execution/logistics (Turkey LD demonstrates downside of in-scope shipping).
- Large-generator ramp dependent on 15-16 month machine-tool delivery — slip risk; revenue contribution only FY29.
- NPCIL/nuclear domestic orders slow and choppy; competition from BHEL, Crompton, imports — no monopoly.
management quality / tone: - Confident, candid, controlled. MD repeatedly defers specifics ("answer in 3 months") on large generators and customer-share questions — disciplined, occasionally guarded. Transparent on the Turkey one-off and copper risk. Notable governance step: first-ever CEO hire (Deepak, ex-L&T Mitsubishi & GE) as #2 — explicit move to "professionalize" management as the company scales. Tone overall buoyant ("buoyant market in all segments," "focus is execution").
non-obvious takeaways:
- TDPS is structurally a "picks-and-shovels" beneficiary of prime-mover OEM capacity doubling by 2030 — 1:1 generator-to-turbine/engine ratio means TDPS volume mechanically tracks OEM expansion; no new generator entrants possible (limited prime-mover base).
- A signed capacity-commitment agreement with INNIO through 2030 (numbers undisclosed but "extremely good") de-risks a large chunk of the gas-engine ramp.
- The large-generator move (up to 200MW) is a TAM step-change competing directly with Siemens, Baker Hughes/Brush, Mitsubishi, Fuji, Toshiba — but monetizes only FY29; near-term it's an optionality story, not earnings.
- SpaceX named as a delivery destination — a marquee data-center/power reference.
- Working-capital intensity is the real constraint on growth, not demand or capacity.

themes.title: Data-Center & AI electrical/cooling buildout
themes.need: AI/data-center capex pulls transformers, switchgear, gensets, HVAC/cooling, optical and cabling AND a new high-margin cooling supply chain. CUMMINSIND flags DC at ~30-35% of domestic powergen with a demand surge since Oct-2025; VENUSPIPES won a ~INR185cr DC-cooling LOI; AEROFLEX building liquid-cooling skids; BLUESTARCO on DC MEP; STLTECH/NETWEB on optical + HPC/AI servers (STLTECH's DC+Enterprise mix hit 21% of Q1FY27 revenue from 1% in FY26 on record INR13,100cr quarterly order intake anchored by a $1.1bn multi-year hyperscaler deal; FY27 EBITDA-margin guide raised 20%->23% and DC+Enterprise mix guide raised 30%->50% of revenue); REDINGTON/DCI/IVALUE on GPU/AI-infra distribution. Q1FY27 added two balance-sheet-scale entrants: HCLTECH is putting up to INR 3,500cr into its own AI-datacenter business with a 50MW long-term ambition ('megawatt isn't the product, it's the anchor'), and RELIANCE disclosed a 168 MW Meta data centre at Jamnagar built on its own balance sheet.
themes.driver: DC cooling LOIs converting (VENUSPIPES, AEROFLEX); hyperscaler/colo India capex (CUMMINSIND gensets, BLUESTARCO MEP); STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler optical-connectivity deal and 2.4x QoQ order-book jump to INR18,618cr; GPU/AI-infra orders.

themes.title: Capital-goods & machine-tool import-substitution
themes.need: Atmanirbhar machine-tool and heavy-engineering localization is supply-constrained against import-substituting demand. JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.
themes.driver: Capacity expansion going live (JYOTICNC); defence/EMS order conversion; US-reshoring export demand (ELGIEQUIP).
